title: Week 8 Warm-Ups
intro: Three short review questions each day: two free-response and one multiple-choice. Every question comes from a section completed before the section scheduled for that day.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A delivery robot rolls 84 m through a school hallway in 14 s. Calculate its average speed in m/s. Does that value prove the robot moved at exactly that speed for the entire trip? Explain briefly.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A backpack stays on the seat of a moving school bus. Describe its motion relative to the bus seat and relative to a person standing at the bus stop. Explain why both descriptions can be correct.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A lab cart has a 24 N push to the right and 9 N of friction to the left. What is its net horizontal force?
choices: 33 N to the right
15 N to the left
24 N to the right
15 N to the right
0 N

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A cyclist rides north at 4 m/s, turns around, and then rides south at 4 m/s. Compare the cyclist’s speed and velocity before and after the turn. Which one changes?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A storage bin slides right across a rough floor at constant velocity while a student pushes it right. Sketch only the horizontal forces on the bin. How do their arrow lengths compare, and why?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A scooter’s speedometer reads 8 m/s at one instant. Over a 15 s trip, it travels 90 m. Which statement is correct?
choices: Average speed = 8 m/s; instantaneous speed = 8 m/s
Average speed = 6 m/s; instantaneous speed at that moment = 8 m/s
Average speed = 8 m/s; instantaneous speed = 6 m/s
Average speed = 90 m/s
The average speed cannot be calculated

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A skateboarder moves straight east and speeds up from 3 m/s to 15 m/s in 4 s. Calculate the average acceleration, including units and direction.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: In a toy-car ramp video, the car takes 0.50 s to cover the first 1 ft and 0.25 s to cover the last 1 ft. Find the average speed for each interval in ft/s. What do the results tell you about the car’s motion?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A scooter is traveling east but slowing down in a straight line. In which direction is its acceleration?
choices: East
There is no acceleration
West
Upward
Its acceleration must point in the direction it is moving

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: An RC car moves east. At 0 s its velocity is 2 m/s; at 2 s it is 6 m/s; at 4 s it is 10 m/s. Calculate its average acceleration from 0 to 4 s. What pattern in the data supports your answer?

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: Two students pull on a cart with equal forces of 18 N in opposite directions. The cart is already moving steadily to the right. Find the net horizontal force and predict whether it must stop. Explain.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A toy car moves around a circular track at a steady speed. Why is it still accelerating?
choices: Its direction, and therefore its velocity, keeps changing.
Its speed must increase around every curve.
It is accelerating only when it passes the starting line.
An object must stop to accelerate.
Circular motion has no velocity.

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A bicycle travels east at 10 m/s, then slows to 4 m/s east in 3 s. Choose east as positive. Calculate its average acceleration and explain what the negative sign means.

questions.topic: Average speed for a round trip

instances.label: Original
instances.stem_html: A runner travels 60 m to a cone and 60 m back to the starting line. The whole trip takes 40 s. Find the runner’s average speed. Why is this speed not zero even though the runner ends where they started?

instances.label: Original
choices: A bike speeds up in a straight line.
A car slows down on a straight road.
A roller coaster turns at steady speed.
A ball reverses its direction.
A robot moves straight east at a constant 5 m/s.
